strengths: Addresses a highly relevant and challenging problem in embodied AI: generating interactive, high-density, and physically plausible 3D tabletop layouts.

Proposes a well-designed, decoupled alignment approach that separates rotation (using a Differentiable Rotation Optimizer with a tri-modal loss) from translation and scale (using a Top-view Spatial Alignment mechanism).
Acheives outstanding results on collision reduction, bringing scene-level collision rates down to 7.69% compared to the 67-98% observed in current state-of-the-art baselines.

Presents a very thorough experimental section, featuring strong baselines, real-world photo testing, scene editing extensions, a large-scale user study (128 participants), and physical robotic manipulation demonstrations in Isaac Sim.
weaknesses: High computational cost and latency: Generating a single tabletop scene with 9 objects takes approximately 32 minutes on an RTX 4090, which may limit its immediate applicability in real-time or closed-loop pipelines.

Heavy reliance on a complex cascade of pre-trained foundation models (GroundedSAM-v2, Hunyuan3D, Seedream, ChatGPT), making the framework highly dependent on API availability and the performance of external black-box models.

Generating a top-view image via a text-to-image/image-to-image diffusion model (TSA stage) is prone to hallucinations or perspective distortion, which could introduce spatial layout inaccuracies for highly complex or occluded scenes.

strengths: Addresses a highly relevant and practical task for embodied AI: creating simulation-ready, interactive, and collision-free tabletop 3D scenes.
The proposed pipeline is modular and versatile, successfully handling both text-to-scene and single-image-to-scene inputs, as well as supporting downstream applications like scene editing.
Provides comprehensive evaluations, including quantitative comparisons against multiple baselines, multi-dimensional GPT-4o evaluations, user studies, and physical verification in Isaac Sim.
The paper is well-written, with clear figures, stage-wise visual breakdowns, and highly detailed supplementary materials including prompt templates and efficiency analyses.
weaknesses: Extremely high computational latency: generating a single tabletop scene with 9 objects takes approximately 32 minutes on an NVIDIA RTX 4090. This severe bottleneck restricts its practical utility for large-scale synthetic data generation in reinforcement learning or real-time simulation.

Limited technical/algorithmic novelty: the framework acts largely as an engineering pipeline combining existing foundation models (ChatGPT, GroundedSAM-v2, Hunyuan3D, Seedream). The novel components (DRO and TSA) are heavily dependent on these models working perfectly.

The rotation optimization (DRO) is simplified to a single degree-of-freedom (yaw rotation around the vertical axis). This is a strong assumption that fails for tilted, overturned, or diagonally stacked objects commonly found in cluttered tabletop environments.

Heavy reliance on generative hallucination: synthesizing a novel 'top-view' image and performing 'generative completion' on occluded objects can easily introduce visual hallucinations, style drifts, and physical inconsistencies that propagate through the pose and scale estimation phases.
Scale estimation relies heavily on LLM 'commonsense' physical size querying, which can be highly inaccurate or biased for non-standard, custom, or stylized assets.

strengths: Highly relevant and well-motivated task addressing high-density tabletop layouts, which are critical yet challenging for robotic simulation and embodied AI.

The proposed Pose and Scale Alignment elegantly decouples the complex 3D recovery task into two manageable stages: a Differentiable Rotation Optimizer (DRO) and a Top-view Spatial Alignment (TSA) mechanism.

Utilizing a multimodal generative model for completion of occluded parts instead of naive inpainting is a smart design choice that significantly improves the downstream per-instance 3D reconstruction.
Comprehensive evaluation showing outstanding results, especially the significantly lower collision rates compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
Demonstrates excellent extension capabilities, including real-world image reconstruction, style-agnostic generation, and downstream robotic pick-and-place execution in Isaac Sim.
weaknesses: High Computational Latency: As shown in the efficiency analysis, the pipeline takes about 32 minutes to generate a single scene with 9 objects. This limits the practicality of the framework for large-scale or real-time simulation data generation.

Heavy Dependence on Top-View Synthesis: The translation and scale estimation relies on a synthesized orthographic top view. Single-view perspective to orthographic top-view synthesis is highly challenging, and generative models can frequently hallucinate or distort the relative positions and counts of dense objects.

Cascading Failure Risk: Since the framework is a training-free, multi-stage modular pipeline, any errors in the early stages (e.g., segmentation, completion, or LLM size estimation) will compound and directly degrade the final 3D scene assembly.

Inherent Ambiguities in LLM-based Size Priors: Relying on the MLLM's common-sense size database can fail for non-standard, stylized, or customized objects whose proportions differ significantly from average category dimensions.

strengths: Practical and High-Impact Focus: The paper addresses a critical bottleneck in robot learning—namely, the lack of diverse, high-fidelity, and physically plausible tabletop simulation environments for large-scale data synthesis.

Decoupled Layout Optimization: Separating the layout recovery into a Differentiable Rotation Optimizer (DRO) for yaw orientation and a Top-View Spatial Alignment (TSA) module with physical priors is a clever design that effectively addresses depth ambiguity and single-view occlusion.

Thorough System-Level Evaluation: The paper provides a very comprehensive evaluation, including visual fidelity metrics, physical plausibility metrics (Col_O, Col_S, Support Stability, Dynamic Settling Stability), a large-scale user study (128 participants), and extensive ablations.

Real-World Robot Validation: Demonstrating zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real policy transfer on a physical AgileX PiPER robot arm is a strong addition that validates the practical value and accuracy of the generated scenes.
weaknesses: Pipeline Integration Complexity vs. Algorithmic Novelty: The proposed method is highly dependent on a chain of external models and APIs (ChatGPT, Seedream, GroundedSAM-v2, Hunyuan3D-3.0). While the integration and layout optimization are well-engineered, the lack of a newly trained core model may be viewed by some as limiting the theoretical visual novelty.

Lack of Latency/Efficiency Analysis: Given the multi-stage nature of the pipeline (including multiple independent Image-to-3D generations, MLLM queries, and gradient-descent differentiable rendering per object), the computational time required to generate a scene could be substantial. The paper lacks a quantitative analysis of scene generation latency.

Cascading Error Sensitivity: The system's performance is tightly bound to individual upstream modules. For example, if GroundedSAM misses an object or Hunyuan3D produces a highly distorted geometry, the downstream DRO/TSA stages may fail. A systematic discussion or experiment on how the pipeline handles sub-module failures would strengthen the paper.

Structural Constraints: The spatial alignment mechanism assumes typical flat tabletop setups with vertical stacking relationships. Its performance on more complex structures (such as nested objects, narrow containers, shelves, or cabinets) remains unverified.

strengths: Elegant decoupling of layout estimation into a Differentiable Rotation Optimizer (DRO) and a Top-View Spatial Alignment (TSA) module, successfully resolving persistent issues like object interpenetration and scale mismatch in prior 3D scene generators.
A training-free and automated framework that bridges generative 3D computer vision and active robotic simulation, showing high value as a scalable data engine.
Strong practical validation via zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real (real2sim2real) policy transfer on a physical robotic arm (AgileX PiPER) across multiple tasks.
Extensive quantitative evaluation, including standard perceptual metrics, physics-based stability indicators, a large-scale user study (128 participants), and comprehensive ablations.
weaknesses: High dependency on multiple black-box generative models (Seedream, Hunyuan3D-3.0, GroundedSAM-v2, and ChatGPT), which introduces potential error propagation and vulnerability to upstream failure modes.

Synthesizing a top-view image (Itop) via a generative model poses consistency risks; generative hallucination in the top-view could lead to physical layout inconsistencies compared to the original perspective photo.
Lacks a detailed analysis of the optimization runtime and computational overhead, which is particularly relevant given the iterative multi-modal gradient descent in DRO and multiple MLLM API calls.

Simplified estimation of key physical properties (e.g., friction, mass, and center of mass) relies on templates/commonsense priors, which can lead to a reality gap in highly contact-sensitive tasks like multi-object stacking.

strengths: The paper addresses a highly important and practical bottleneck in Embodied AI and robotics: generating high-fidelity, instance-level, and physically plausible interactive 3D simulation environments for tabletop manipulation data synthesis.

The proposed decoupled pose and scale alignment approach is technically elegant and well-motivated. Separating rotation (optimized using visual/renderer features via DRO) from translation and scale (constrained via synthesized top-views and stacking priors via TSA) effectively resolves the common physical inconsistencies (e.g., interpenetration, floating objects) seen in general 3D scene generators.

The evaluation is exceptionally thorough. Beyond standard visual/perceptual metrics (LPIPS, DINOv2, CLIP) and user studies, the paper reports crucial physics-based metrics such as Support Stability (SS) and Dynamic Settling Stability (DSS), showing massive improvements over existing baselines.

The inclusion of a zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real (Real-to-Sim-to-Real) policy transfer experiment on a physical AgileX PiPER robot arm successfully demonstrates the real-world utility of the generated environments for policy learning.
weaknesses: The entire pipeline relies heavily on a complex chain of external foundations and proprietary/large APIs (such as ChatGPT, Seedream, GroundedSAM-v2, and Hunyuan3D-3.0). While being training-free is an advantage, the cumulative runtime latency and API dependency might limit high-throughput scene generation and scalability.

The Top-View Spatial Alignment (TSA) relies significantly on the synthesis of a perfect orthographic top-view image ($I_{top}$) by a generative model (Seedream). Since perspective-to-orthographic translation is challenging, any hallucinations or spatial inaccuracies in $I_{top}$ could cascade and lead to severe alignment failures. The paper would benefit from a sensitivity analysis regarding errors in the synthesized top-view.

The method currently assumes relatively flat, single-support tabletop geometries and simple vertical stacking. It remains unclear how well the pipeline handles complex, non-convex container geometries (e.g., placing objects inside boxes with lids) or multi-level support surfaces (such as shelves or racks) where top-view projections fail to capture the full 3D layout.
